facts.statement: The species Confuciusornis sanctus was formally described in 1995.

facts.statement: The generic name Confuciusornis combines the name of the philosopher Confucius with the Greek word for bird.
facts.quote: The generic name combines the philosopher Confucius with Greek ὄρνις (ornis), "bird".

facts.statement: The holotype specimen is catalogued as IVPP V10918.

facts.quote: At one time forty individuals were discovered on a surface of about 100 m2

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that mass deaths of Confuciusornis flocks were caused by volcanic eruptions releasing ash, heat, or poisonous gas.
facts.quote: This has been explained as the result of entire flocks of birds being simultaneously killed by ash, heat or poisonous gas following the volcanic eruptions

facts.statement: It is debated whether the paratype specimens definitively belong to the species Confuciusornis sanctus due to a lack of overlapping bones with the holotype.

facts.statement: The Yixian and Jiufotang Formations are now dated to the Lower Cretaceous, between 131 and 120 million years ago.
facts.quote: Later, both formations have been dated to the Lower Cretaceous (Barremian to Aptian stages, 131–120 million years ago)

facts.statement: Five additional species were formally named and described after the initial description of Confuciusornis sanctus.
facts.quote: Since the description of Confuciusornis sanctus, five additional species have been formally named and described.

facts.statement: It is debated whether differences between named species of Confuciusornis represent distinct species or just individual variation within a single species.
facts.quote: As with many other fossil genera, species are difficult to define, as differences between species can often not be readily distinguished from variation that occurs within a species.

facts.statement: Only the species Confuciusornis sanctus is universally accepted by scientists, while others are considered synonyms.
facts.quote: In the case of Confuciusornis, only C. sanctus is universally accepted.

facts.statement: Confuciusornis chuonzhous was named by Hou in 1997 based on specimen IVPP V10919, which was originally a paratype of C. sanctus.
facts.quote: Confuciusornis chuonzhous was named by Hou in 1997 based on specimen IVPP V10919, originally a paratype of C. sanctus.

facts.statement: Confuciusornis suniae was named by Hou in 1997 based on specimen IVPP V11308.
facts.quote: Confuciusornis suniae, named by Hou in the same 1997 publication, was based on specimen IVPP V11308.

facts.statement: Confuciusornis dui was named by Hou and colleagues in 1999.
facts.quote: Confuciusornis dui was named by Hou and colleagues in 1999.

facts.statement: The holotype of Confuciusornis dui (IVPP V11553) is a nearly complete adult skeleton featuring long tail feathers and an impression of a horny beak.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen (IVPP V11553) is a nearly complete skeleton of an adult that includes a pair of long tail feathers and the impression of the horny beak.

facts.statement: Confuciusornis feducciai was named in 2009 by Zhang Fucheng and colleagues to honor ornithologist Alan Feduccia.
facts.quote: Confuciusornis feducciai was named in 2009 by Zhang Fucheng and colleagues, the specific name honouring ornithologist Alan Feduccia.

facts.statement: The holotype of Confuciusornis feducciai (D2454) was discovered at Sihetun and is housed at the Dalian Natural Museum.
facts.quote: The holotype, D2454, was discovered at the Sihetun locality and is kept at the Dalian Natural Museum.

facts.statement: The genus Jinzhouornis, named by Hou in 2002, is now considered a junior synonym of Confuciusornis based on morphometric analysis.
facts.quote: In 2002 Hou named the genus Jinzhouornis, but Chiappe et al. (2018) and Wang et al. (2018) showed that this genus is a junior synonym of Confuciusornis based on morphometry and examination of known confuciusornithiform specimens.

facts.statement: Confuciusornis was roughly the size of a modern crow, measuring about 50 cm in length with a wingspan of up to 70 cm.
facts.quote: Confuciusornis was about the size of a modern crow, with a total length of 50 cm and a wingspan of up to 70 cm.

facts.statement: The body weight of Confuciusornis has been estimated to range from 0.2 kg to 0.5 kg.
facts.quote: Its body weight has been estimated to have been as much as 0.5 kg, or as little as 0.2 kg.

facts.statement: Confuciusornis feducciai was approximately one-third longer than average specimens of C. sanctus.
facts.quote: C. feducciai was about a third longer than average specimens of C. sanctus.

facts.statement: Confuciusornis exhibits a combination of both primitive (basal) and advanced (derived) traits.
facts.quote: Confuciusornis shows a mix of basal and derived traits.

facts.statement: Confuciusornis was more advanced than Archaeopteryx due to its short pygostyle and bony sternum, but more primitive than modern birds because it retained large forelimb claws, a skull with a closed eye-socket, and a small breastbone.
facts.quote: It was more "advanced" or derived than Archaeopteryx in possessing a short tail with a pygostyle (a bone formed from a series of short, fused tail vertebrae) and a bony sternum (breastbone), but more basal or "primitive" than modern birds in retaining large claws on the forelimbs, having a primitive skull with a closed eye-socket, and a relatively small breastbone.

facts.statement: Early interpretations exaggerated primitive traits, such as when Hou assumed in 1995 that the animal had a long tail and mistook jaw bone grooves for teeth.
facts.quote: At first the number of basal characteristics was exaggerated: Hou assumed in 1995 that a long tail was present and mistook grooves in the jaw bones for small degenerated teeth.

facts.statement: The skull of Confuciusornis was near triangular in side view with a robust, toothless, and pointed beak.
facts.quote: The skull was near triangular in side view, and the toothless beak was robust and pointed.

facts.statement: The skull of Confuciusornis was robust with deep jaws, particularly the mandible.
facts.quote: The skull was rather robust, with deep jaws, especially the mandible.

facts.statement: The orbit of the Confuciusornis skull was large, round, and contained scleral plates.
facts.quote: The orbit was large, round, and contained scleral plates (the bony support inside the eye).

facts.statement: A C. sanctus specimen has an upper beak margin that is almost straight with a tip slightly hooked downwards.
facts.quote: a C. sanctus specimen (IVPP V12352) has an upper margin that is almost straight, and a tip that appears to be slightly hooked downwards.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Confuciusornis possesses an ancestral diapsid skull; while it was considered the first known bird with this trait in the late 1990s, a 2018 study concluded the temporal configuration was an autapomorphic trait unique to the group.
facts.quote: Confuciusornis was considered the first known bird with an ancestral diapsid skull (with two temporal fenestrae on each side of the skull) in the late 1990s, but in 2018, Elzanowski and colleagues concluded that the configuration seen in the temporal region of confuciusornithids was autapomorphic (a unique trait that evolved secondarily rather than having been retained from a primitive condition) for their group.

facts.statement: Confuciusornis specimens show a variable number of neck vertebrae, ranging from eight to nine.
facts.quote: The various specimens seem to have a variable number of neck vertebrae, some showing eight, others nine.

facts.statement: Confuciusornis had at least twelve back vertebrae.
facts.quote: There were at least twelve back vertebrae.

facts.statement: Confuciusornis possessed a synsacrum formed by seven fused sacral vertebrae.
facts.quote: Seven sacral vertebrae were fused into a synsacrum.

facts.statement: In 1999, Chiappe and colleagues reported that Confuciusornis had seven free tail vertebrae, whereas earlier descriptions counted four or five.
facts.quote: Although earlier descriptions had counted four or five "free", not fused, tail vertebrae, Chiappe e.a. in 1999 reported seven of them.

facts.statement: The tail of Confuciusornis ended in a pygostyle, which is a complete fusion of the last vertebrae.
facts.quote: The tail ended in a pygostyle, a complete fusion of the last vertebrae.

facts.statement: Confuciusornis possessed an exceptionally large humerus.
facts.quote: Confuciusornis had an exceptionally large humerus (upper arm bone).

facts.statement: The furcula of Confuciusornis was a simple curved bar lacking a hypocleidium, similar to that of Archaeopteryx.
facts.quote: The furcula or wishbone, like that of Archaeopteryx, was a simple curved bar lacking a pointed process at the back, a hypocleidium.

facts.statement: The sternum of Confuciusornis was relatively broad with a low keel that was raised at the back end.
facts.quote: The sternum was relatively broad and had a low keel which was raised at the back end.

facts.statement: Confuciusornis had a sideways shoulder joint orientation, preventing it from lifting its wings high above its back.
facts.quote: The orientation of the shoulder joint was sideways, instead of angled upward as in modern birds; this means that Confuciusornis was unable to lift its wings high above its back.

facts.statement: The finger phalange formula of Confuciusornis was 2-3-4-0-0.
facts.quote: The formula of the finger phalanges was 2-3-4-0-0.

facts.statement: The toe phalange formula of Confuciusornis was 2-3-4-5-0.
facts.quote: The formula of the toe phalanges was 2-3-4-5-0.

facts.statement: The wing feathers of Confuciusornis were long and appeared modern.
facts.quote: The wing feathers of Confuciusornis were long and modern in appearance.

facts.statement: In a 0.5-kilogram individual, the primary wing feathers of Confuciusornis reached 20.7 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: The primary wing feathers of a 0.5-kilogram individual reached 20.7 centimetres in length.

facts.statement: Confuciusornis lacked an alula, or "bastard wing", unlike some more advanced birds.
facts.quote: Unlike some more advanced birds, Confuciusornis lacked an alula, or "bastard wing".

facts.statement: The forearm bones of Confuciusornis lacked quill knobs or bony attachment points for feather ligaments.
facts.quote: The forearm bones lacked any indication of quill knobs (papillae ulnares), or bony attachment points for the feather ligaments.

facts.statement: Most of the tail feathers of Confuciusornis formed a ribbon-like sheet about six millimeters wide.
facts.quote: Rather, most of the feather formed a ribbon-like sheet, about six millimetres wide.

facts.statement: Many individuals of Confuciusornis lacked the two long tail feathers, possibly due to sexual dimorphism.
facts.quote: Many individuals of Confuciusornis lacked even these two tail feathers, possibly due to sexual dimorphism.

facts.statement: Laser fluorescence analysis of two specimens revealed details of the soft-tissue anatomy of Confuciusornis.
facts.quote: Laser fluorescence of two Confuciusornis specimens revealed additional details of their soft-tissue anatomy.

facts.statement: Reticulate scales covered the underside of the Confuciusornis foot, which supported large fleshy pads, though interphalangeal pads were small or absent.
facts.quote: Reticulate scales covered the underside of the foot, and the phalanges and metatarsals supported large, fleshy pads, although the interphalangeal pads were either small or entirely absent.

facts.statement: Based on melanosomes, Confuciusornis likely had grey, red/brown, and black feathers, resembling a modern zebra finch.
facts.quote: This indicated that Confuciusornis had hues of grey, red/brown and black, possibly something like the modern zebra finch.

facts.statement: Male Confuciusornis likely had long tail feathers that were dark along their entire length.
facts.quote: The long tail feathers of male specimens would have also been dark in color along their entire length.

facts.statement: Hou assigned Confuciusornis to the family Confuciusornithidae in 1995.
facts.quote: Hou assigned Confuciusornis to the Confuciusornithidae in 1995.

facts.statement: Hou later concluded that Confuciusornis was the sister taxon of Enantiornithes within the group Sauriurae.
facts.quote: Later he understood that Confuciusornis was not an enantiornithean but concluded it was the sister taxon of the Enantiornithes, within a larger Sauriurae.

facts.statement: Chiappe criticized Hou's placement of Confuciusornis in Sauriurae, arguing the group was paraphyletic due to insufficient shared traits.
facts.quote: This was heavily criticised by Chiappe who regarded Sauriurae to be paraphyletic as there were insufficient shared traits that indicated that the Confuciusornithidae and the Enantiornithes were closely related.

facts.statement: In 2001, Ji Qiang suggested Confuciusornis was the sister taxon of Ornithothoraces.
facts.quote: In 2001, Ji Qiang suggested an alternative position as the sister taxon of the Ornithothoraces.

facts.statement: A 2002 cladistic analysis by Chiappe confirmed Ji's hypothesis and defined Confuciusornis as the most basal member of the group Pygostylia.
facts.quote: In 2002 Ji's hypothesis was confirmed by a cladistic analysis by Chiappe, who defined a new group: the Pygostylia of which Confuciusornis is by definition the most basal member.

facts.statement: A controversial study suggested Confuciusornis was more closely related to Microraptor and dromaeosaurids than Archaeopteryx, but this was criticized on methodological grounds.
facts.quote: One controversial study concluded that Confuciusornis may be more closely related to Microraptor and other dromaeosaurids than to Archaeopteryx, but this study was criticized on methodological grounds.

facts.statement: Confuciusornis fossils date to the Early Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Cretácico inferior

facts.statement: Confuciusornis were crow-sized prehistoric birds that lived at the end of the Early Cretaceous (approximately 120 million years ago) in what is now China.
facts.quote: Confuciusornis es un género de aves prehistóricas del tamaño de un cuervo, que vivieron a finales del período Cretácico Inferior (hace aproximadamente 120 millones de años) en lo que hoy es China.

facts.statement: Like modern birds, Confuciusornis had a toothless beak.
facts.quote: Al igual que las aves modernas, Confuciusornis tenía un pico sin dientes

facts.statement: The loss of teeth in Confuciusornis likely occurred convergently with that of contemporary birds like Hesperornis and Ichthyornis.
facts.quote: lo que indicaría que la pérdida de ellos ocurrió convergentemente en Confuciusornis y en las aves contemporáneas.

facts.statement: Confuciusornis was the size of a modern crow or pigeon, with a wingspan of up to 70 cm and an estimated weight of up to 1.5 kg or less than 0.2 kg depending on the author.
facts.quote: Confuciusornis tenía el tamaño de un cuervo o una paloma modernos, con una envergadura de hasta 70 cm y un peso estimado de hasta 1,5 kg o menos de 0,2 kg, según diferentes autores.

facts.statement: The beak of Confuciusornis lacked teeth, unlike some other early birds such as Liaoningornis and Yanornis which still possessed teeth.
facts.quote: El cráneo presenta una inusual combinación de características: mientras que el pico de Confuciusornis al igual que el pico de las aves actuales no poseía dientes, otras aves más modernas como Liaoningornis y Yanornis en cambio todavía tenían dientes.

facts.statement: The back of the Confuciusornis head had two pairs of cranial openings (infratemporal and supratemporal) located behind the eye sockets, similar to diapsid reptiles.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, la zona posterior de la cabeza estaba conformada en forma similar que en los reptiles diápsidos: dos pares de aberturas craneanas (infratemporal y supratemporal) se ubicaban por detrás de las aberturas oculares (órbitas).

facts.statement: The sternum of some Confuciusornis specimens had a keel-like structure similar to that of modern birds.
facts.quote: El esternón de algunos de los ejemplares presenta un empeine que tiene alguna semejanza a la quilla que poseen las aves modernas.

facts.statement: Available information does not indicate that Confuciusornis or Archaeopteryx possessed an alula.
facts.quote: La información disponible a la fecha no indica que Confuciusornis y Archaeopteryx tuvieran alula.

facts.statement: Confuciusornis retained functional raptor claws on its thumb and middle finger, while its index finger, which held flight feathers, consisted of flat, broad bones and a smaller claw.
facts.quote: Confuciusornis conserva todavía garras raptoras funcionales en sus dedos pulgar y medio, pero su dedo índice —el dedo que sostiene las plumas de vuelo— se compone de huesos planos y amplios y una garra menor.

facts.statement: Fossil studies show that Confuciusornis had an exceptionally long humerus.
facts.quote: El estudio de los fósiles de Confuciusornis muestra que tenía un húmero excepcionalmente largo.

facts.statement: Near the shoulder, the humerus of Confuciusornis had a large bone plate with a characteristic oval opening that may have helped reduce the bone's weight.
facts.quote: Posee en su extremo superior cerca del hombro una gran placa ósea con una abertura oval característica, que podría haber contribuido a reducir el peso del hueso.

facts.statement: Confuciusornis differed from Archaeopteryx, Rahonavis, and Jeholornis by having a shortened tail and a pygostyle formed by the fusion of the last tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: Confuciornis (y Sapeornis) se diferencian de Archaeopteryx, Rahonavis y Jeholornis por tener los primeros una importante innovación consistente en el acortamiento de la cola y el desarrollo de un pigóstilo mediante la fusión de las últimas vértebras de la cola.

facts.statement: The glenoid joint (shoulder) of Confuciusornis was oriented laterally rather than dorsally as in modern birds, meaning it could not raise its wings above its back.
facts.quote: La orientación de la coyuntura glenoide (hombro) era lateral, en vez de en ángulo dorsal como en las aves modernas; esto significa que Confuciornis era incapaz de levantar sus alas por encima de su espalda.

facts.statement: Some Confuciusornis specimens had long feathers on their lower limbs, giving them "four wings," a feature also found in Sapeornis, Cathayornis, and Yanornis.
facts.quote: En algunos ejemplares se han encontrado plumas largas en las extremidades inferiores, teniendo por tanto "cuatro alas"; lo mismo se ha encontrado en ejemplares de Sapeornis, Cathayornis y Yanornis.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the oval opening in the humerus of Confuciusornis was a unique trait or more widespread among early birds, as the similar feature was later found in Sapeornis.
facts.quote: La función de esta abertura no está clara para un autapomorfismo, y se pensaba era una característica exclusiva de este tipo. Sin embargo en el 2002 se describió el ave Sapeornis que proviene también de las rocas del macizo Jehol, y posee una abertura similar en el antebrazo. Por lo tanto podría ser posible que esta característica estuviera más difundida entre las aves tempranas que lo que inicialmente se pensó.
